item.title: Episode 1: Mud, Canals, and the First Ledgers
item.itunes:title: Episode 1: Mud, Canals, and the First Ledgers
item.itunes:author: Amy & Sam
item.description: Over five thousand years ago in southern Mesopotamia, cities like Uruk and Ur put tens of thousands of strangers on dry river mud with almost no timber or stone. Amy and Sam unpack how gravity canals turned wrong-season floods into barley surplus, how temple devotion, crisis lugal leaders, dusu work shifts, and še-ba grain rations created early politics and taxes, how proto-cuneiform ledgers (like Kushim's three-year barley record) kept counts straight, how mudbrick ziggurats, wool-for-copper caravans, and sealed clay-envelope contracts held cities together—and why trapped salt slowly pushed farming north. Theme music: J. S. Bach — Suite in E Major, BWV 1006a: Gavotte en Rondeau (solo guitar by Emilio Antonucci, Jamendo #108621, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0).
